dedupe_keys.name: esa cream collision risk estimation and automated mitigation ground pilots and in orbit demonstrations

description: CREAM, the Collision Risk Estimation and Automated Mitigation project, is an ESA effort to automate how satellite operators assess conjunctions with other satellites and debris, plan avoidance manoeuvres and coordinate with each other. It sits in ESA's Space Safety Programme, started in 2020 and is built by GMV and Guardtime, with GMV integrating the prototype components on one platform. Coverage is orbit-wide, with over 11 000 active satellites and 1.2 million debris pieces above 1 cm as the backdrop. The ground system can already raise alerts and generate avoidance manoeuvres, and a mediation service is planned for disputes between operators; piggyback missions and a dedicated in-orbit demonstration follow. Format and access: an ESA web story of 12 August 2025, free to read, with no data release. Licence: ESA website terms, not read. Caveats: it is a project announcement, without measured results, and the system is still ground based. It supports resilience and operations studies of how automated coordination could shape orbital collision risk. Related catalogue records are the ESA collision avoidance challenge conjunction dataset and the TraCSS verification dataset.

outcomes: The ground-based prototype already generates collision alerts and actionable avoidance manoeuvres for the ground segment and supports coordination between parties; the project enters an expanded pilot phase, with in-orbit demonstrations being prepared. The page reports no measured reduction in operator workload or false alerts.
